We are a passionate and enthusiastic team excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are interested in space exploration, science, technology, innovation, and solving real-world problems through creative ideas. Our goal is to collaborate, learn from each other, and develop innovative solutions using data, research, and technology.

We welcome people who are curious, creative, motivated, and willing to work together.
summary:
MonsoonLens is an interactive climate trend investigation dashboard developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It uses monthly climate data from NASA POWER to explore long-term changes in temperature, precipitation and relative humidity across selected locations in India, including Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Kozhikode, Bengaluru, Mumbai and New Delhi.

The platform transforms monthly observations into annual climate indicators and visualizes changes through interactive charts. It includes annual temperature trends, accumulated rainfall, June–September monsoon rainfall and annual relative humidity. Users can compare multiple locations, examine trend estimates and statistical significance, and explore geographical patterns through an interactive map.

By making climate data easier to visualize and compare, MonsoonLens helps users investigate how environmental indicators change over time and how these patterns differ between regions. It uses NASA POWER data to make Earth system trends more accessible and understandable.
details:
MonsoonLens – Earth System Trend Detective

What does the project do and how does it work?

MonsoonLens is an interactive climate trend investigation dashboard that helps users explore how climate indicators change over time and differ across geographical locations in India.

The project retrieves monthly climate data from NASA POWER through its API, focusing on three indicators: air temperature (T2M), precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) and relative humidity (RH2M). The monthly data is processed into annual indicators and presented through interactive visualizations.

Users can select a study location and time period, investigate annual temperature trends, accumulated rainfall, June–September monsoon rainfall and annual relative humidity. The dashboard also provides trend estimates, statistical analysis, comparisons between multiple locations and an interactive map showing the selected study regions.

What benefits does it have?

MonsoonLens makes climate data easier to understand without requiring users to download datasets or perform statistical calculations themselves. It brings multiple climate indicators together in one accessible interface and allows users to compare geographical differences. This helps students, educators and other interested users explore environmental patterns using NASA's Earth science data.

What is the intended impact?

The intended impact is to improve awareness and understanding of regional climate variability and long-term environmental changes. By making Earth science data more accessible, MonsoonLens encourages data-driven exploration, environmental education and curiosity about interconnected Earth systems.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed primarily using Python. Streamlit was used to build the interactive dashboard, Pandas and NumPy for data processing, Plotly for interactive charts and geographical visualizations, SciPy for statistical analysis, and Requests for retrieving data from the NASA POWER API. Development and testing were performed on a Linux-based computer. No dedicated external hardware is required.

How is the project creative?

MonsoonLens combines several climate indicators, statistical trend analysis, geographical visualization and multi-location comparison in a single investigation tool. Rather than presenting climate data as isolated tables, it allows users to interactively explore relationships between time, location and environmental change. Its focus on Indian locations also provides a regional perspective on climate patterns.

What factors did the team consider?

The development considered data availability, reliability of monthly observations, missing values, appropriate annual aggregation methods, ease of use and geographical coverage. Minimum valid-month requirements were applied to annual calculations to reduce misleading results from incomplete data. Rainfall accumulation accounts for the number of days in each month, while annual humidity uses day-weighted averaging. Statistical significance is interpreted cautiously because correlation does not establish causation, and autocorrelation may affect p-values.

MonsoonLens aims to turn publicly available NASA climate data into an accessible and interactive experience for investigating changes in our environment.
